title: Study finds many young men feel lonely, disconnected, shut out of the American dream | Institute for Family Studies
gist: A short news round-up of the second installment of IFS's 'America's Demoralized Men' study — a YouGov survey of 2,000 men aged 18-29 finding that more than half feel lonely or isolated at least some of the time, nearly half lack a sense of community, and many see the American dream as out of reach. The key nuance is that these men still want marriage, fatherhood, and meaningful work; the gap is between aspiration and attainment.

themes.theme: Loneliness and disconnection among young American men

insights.claim: More than half of US young men report feeling lonely or isolated at least some of the time and nearly half lack a sense of community, per a nationally representative survey of 2,000 men aged 18 to 29.
insights.speaker: Institute for Family Studies
insights.so_what: Majority-level loneliness in the prime household-formation cohort is a leading indicator for marriage rates, fertility, and demand for parasocial and digital-companionship products.

insights.claim: The demand side is intact: researchers found a generation that still desires marriage, fatherhood, and meaningful work but struggles to achieve those goals, meaning the deficit is in attainment rather than aspiration.
insights.speaker: Institute for Family Studies
insights.so_what: If preferences for family formation have not changed, fertility and marriage declines are a friction problem that policy or economics could plausibly reverse — a materially different forecast than a preference shift.
insights.quote: a generation that still desires marriage, fatherhood, and meaningful work but often struggles to achieve those goals

insights.claim: The study's second installment scopes four domains together — social lives, mental health, civic engagement, and online habits — signalling that IFS treats digital behavior as a candidate mechanism alongside social and civic withdrawal.
insights.speaker: Institute for Family Studies
insights.so_what: Watch for the causal argument to land on screen time and online substitution, which would put it alongside the broader smartphone-and-adolescence research shaping platform regulation.
